goal: Change what happens when unlocking the wallet fails right after encryption succeeds, to avoid a misleading error message telling the user encryption failed when it actually succeeded.
reviewability: Code diff is trivial but the approach itself is in dispute and likely to change
A maintainer flagged a bigger correctness problem July 17 that has gone unanswered for weeks
agreement: Maintainer objection: current fix does not go far enough and may mask a catastrophic wallet-corruption case (achow101)
Author partially agrees logging is wrong and floats other options but has not implemented a fix (vicjuma)

categories.name: wallet
why: P3 because the edge case (unlock failing immediately after successful encryption) is rare but touches fund safety: a maintainer says this could indicate wallet corruption and lost funds if mishandled.
The current one-line fix (log instead of return false) is disputed as insufficient rather than wrong in intent, so the underlying question needs a decision before code review matters.

result.summary: This PR changes CWallet::EncryptWallet so that a failed post-encryption Unlock() call logs a message instead of returning false, aiming to stop a misleading 'Failed to encrypt the wallet' RPC error being shown after encryption has actually already succeeded. The diff is a single line. The description walks through a reproduction showing the current misleading error text via bitcoin-cli.
result.problem: Users who successfully encrypt a wallet but then hit a rare unlock failure inside the same call currently see 'Error: Failed to encrypt the wallet,' even though encryption did complete, which misinforms operators about the wallet's actual state.

open_concerns: achow101 (maintainer) argues that an unlock failure right after successful encryption may signal wallet corruption and possible fund loss, and that logging a warning is not sufficient; the wallet should probably be prevented from further use (Assert or similar).
No implemented fix addresses achow101's concern; author has floated an enum-based return type or an internal RPC error but not implemented either.
katesalazar questioned whether this is a 'lazy workaround' rather than a thorough fix and drew a comparison to PR #28333 (GetDatabase().Rewrite()) which the author says is unrelated.

categories.name: wallet
categories.evidence: Directly modifies CWallet::EncryptWallet in src/wallet/wallet.cpp, changing failure-handling behavior after wallet encryption.
categories.rationale: A maintainer (achow101) flagged that the scenario this PR touches, unlock failing immediately after successful encryption, could indicate wallet corruption with potential fund loss, calling the correct response 'catastrophic failure' handling rather than a log line. That raises the ceiling on this category above a pure cosmetic error-message fix, but the scenario is rare and the current PR's approach is explicitly rejected as insufficient, so it remains worthwhile-but-deferrable pending a real design decision rather than category-critical today.

uncertainties: Whether the unlock-fails-after-encryption scenario is purely theoretical or has been observed in practice; this affects how urgent the fund-safety angle really is.
Whether achow101's objection should be read as a blocking Approach NACK (pushing this toward Blocked) versus an open design question; treated here as Disputed since the author engaged same day.
result.card: This PR changes a single line in CWallet::EncryptWallet so that a failed post-encryption Unlock() call logs a message instead of returning false, aiming to stop a misleading 'Failed to encrypt the wallet' RPC error after encryption actually succeeded. The author's own repro shows bitcoin-cli reporting the wrong error code (-16) in this edge case. Maintainer achow101 rejected the fix as insufficient, arguing that an unlock failure right after successful encryption may signal wallet corruption and possible fund loss, and that the wallet should be prevented from further use rather than just logged; the author partially agreed but has not pushed an alternative fix since 2026-08-17. Reviewing the current diff is likely wasted effort until the approach is settled. No stated dependencies or blocking PRs.
